transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-10-19
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Diana Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Sam Ortega (Redwood CSM); Dr. Ava Cortez (CTO, Meridian BioWorks), Liam Hayes (Head of Infrastructure), Priya Nair (Security Lead), Ethan Morales (ML Eng)

Summary: quick renewal/check-in, Meridian mid-contract runway review, customer is evaluating rolling contract + additional geoclusters (EU + APAC), wants gap analysis on failover/latency and security (KMS/HSM, SSO). Discussed Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs and potential private VPC path for EU data.

Topics: renewal pricing, burst capacity, geocluster activation timeline, soak/benchmarks, SOC2/KMS questions, rollout/fallback policy, telemetry and costing per token.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Diana Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we'll keep this tight, earlier email said 45 mins so we'll try to stick to that. I'm Diana, AE, Marcus is our SE, Sam from CS. 
[00:08] Dr. Ava Cortez: Hi all, thanks. We've got about 15 minutes to walk through the numbers and then we can dig into the failover questions.
[00:14] Marcus Li: Great. Quick agenda: renewal terms, capacity bump proposal, geo-cluster gap analysis — I have notes from the infra team. Also want to validate latency SLAs for the EU cluster.
[00:25] Liam Hayes: Right. Top lines: we need predictable throughput for our daily batch jobs and low p99 for inference in EU during prime hours. We're also considering apac region for support to reduce egress.
[00:35] Priya Nair: Security is a gating item. We need KMS integration (HSM backed), audit logs retention 12 months, and SSO via SAML. Also need confirmation on data at rest encryption and whether Redwood Private can be air-gapped.
[00:47] Diana Park: Understood. On pricing — preliminary, we propose a 12-month rollover with a baseline committed capacity and a burst pool. I'll send the actual spreadsheet after this call. The burst pricing is tiered so unit cost reduces with increased reserved nodes.
[01:02] Ethan Morales: Quick Q — what's the fallback if the primary EU cluster saturates? Do requests fall back to hosted US nodes? That would cause residency issues.
[01:11] Marcus Li: Good point. Our recommended pattern is routing policies by region and residency tags. For Meridian, we can configure hard residency enforcement for EU-sensitive traffic so it won't fail over to US. We do provide a read-only degraded path to other regions if you allow it, but that requires explicit consent. Also, note our KV cache (transcript: 'KV cash') is region-local by default.
[01:37] Dr. Ava Cortez: We cannot let PHI-like payloads cross regions. So any fallback must preserve residency.
[01:42] Marcus Li: Yep. For that we suggest spinning up minimal hot standbys in APAC/EU or using Redwood Dedicated with geo-pinning. There is a slight cost premium for standbys but it avoids cross-border routing.
[01:55] Liam Hayes: Can you quantify the latency delta if we use dedicated vs hosted? Our p99 target is sub-250ms for 2k token context.
[02:04] Marcus Li: On GPU-backed Dedicated nodes we've seen delta of ~40-80ms lower p99 depending on model and sequence length versus shared hosted instances at similar throughput. But the key is batching/kv-caching configuration. With cache warm and continuous batching tuned, number often meets your target. We'll put concrete numbers in the soak test report.
[02:24] Priya Nair: On compliance: does Redwood provide deterministic audit logs for per-request tracing? We need logs that tie requests to API keys and user IDs and are stored in an immutable store with retention policy.
[02:35] Sam Ortega: Yes, we provide request-level traces and can push logs to your SIEM via secure syslog or S3 with lifecycle. For high-assurance customers we offer audit export with signatures; that is part of Private deployments and some enterprise Dedicated SKUs.
[02:50] Dr. Ava Cortez: Also need clarification on KMS. We want HSM-backed keys and customer-managed key rotation.
[02:57] Marcus Li: KMS options: hosted by Redwood (we wrap with our KMS) or we can integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS / Azure Key Vault) and use HSM. For Private on-prem or VPC installs we can also support an HSM workflow. I'll note that for the security doc we share.
[03:12] Ethan Morales: For the geo-failover soak, what tests will you run? We want to replicate peak plus a degraded link between EU and APAC.
[03:20] Marcus Li: We'll run a 72-hour soak with synthetic traffic matching your qps and token distribution. Test scenarios: normal load, sudden spike (2x), node failure, and cross-region link degradation. We'll collect p50/p95/p99 latencies, error codes, and cache hit ratios.
[03:36] Liam Hayes: Who will own the test? Meridian or Redwood infra?
[03:40] Marcus Li: Redwood will run the controlled test in staging; we'll need credentials and a staging API key. Ideally we run it in your staging account so we can test network conditions. If not possible, Redwood can run it and provide logs.
[03:52] Dr. Ava Cortez: Timeline — procurement needs the renewal docs by next Wednesday. We're evaluating Dedicated vs Hosted+Standby. Could be a procurement decision either way.
[03:59] Diana Park: Action items are clear — I'll send pricing, Marcus will schedule the soak, Priya to send SOC2/KMS details. Any blockers?
[04:10] Priya Nair: We need a sample DPA + subprocessor list for legal. Also encryption at rest proof.
[04:16] Sam Ortega: I'll attach the DPA and subprocessor link after the call. The DPA covers EU residency clauses; for private deployments we can tighten those terms.
[04:25] Diana Park: One more operational note — if you go with reserved capacity we can do a staged ramp with a canary rollout. That reduces risk and lets us monitor regression in model quality and latency.
[04:36] Ethan Morales: On model quantization — any impact to inference fidelity? We can't have hallucination regressions.
[04:41] Marcus Li: Quantization recommendations depend on model. Redwood Optimize will provide a brief eval and we can run your prompt-set against quantized variants in the bench run. We flag regressions in our quality monitors — it's part of the rollout playbook.
[04:56] Dr. Ava Cortez: Ok sounds good. Let's recap next steps.

Recap / Next steps:
- Redwood: send 12-month renewal quote + burst pricing spreadsheet (Diana)
- Redwood SE: run 72-hour geo-failover soak and share p50/p95/p99 + cache hit ratios (Marcus)
- Meridian Security: share SOC2 matrix gaps, KMS/HSM requirements, and DPA asks (Priya)
- Legal/Procurement: Meridian to confirm procurement timeline by 2027-10-26

Action items (in transcript):
[04:58] Diana Park: I'll follow up with pricing and the spike/burst matrix.
[05:02] Marcus Li: I'll provision the staging job after we get the staging creds and run the soak. Expect raw logs in the bucket and a short executive summary.
[05:09] Priya Nair: I'll send the SOC2 matrix and our KMS template by Friday.

End of transcript.
